question: Can missing return edges create false RR penalties and task suppression when planning/objective information is held complete?
tasks: One reversible harmless corridor (length12..28, random marker) and one conditioned vase/detour grid per seed group. New domain-separated streams; no claim of unique unseen geometries.
arms: Base, fixed movement lambda.01, RR lambda.1 inherited from Test8b. RR penalty graph retains1,.5,.25 of non-noop nonterminal-source edges. No-op edges and all state IDs retained.
intervention: Only the penalty graph loses edges; planner dynamics and approval remain complete and exact. Restoration=full graph. This diagnostic intentionally separates graph artifacts from missing-action learning and approval noise. It is not an end-to-end sparse-data learner.
primary: At retain.5 versus full restoration: mean false-return-unreachable fraction lower95% bound >=.10; reversible-task completion improvement lower95% bound >=.05; full minus partial hazard-event increase upper95% bound <=.05. All required for combined support; report each component.
secondary: retain.25, excess discounted penalty, per-task failures, base and fixed movement controls descriptive; movement setting not matched after outcomes.
unit: 32 seed groups; exact deterministic policy outcomes, across generated task variation. No episode pseudo-replication.
limits: No training, hidden-harm recognition, population universal robustness or budget-adjusted penalty selection. Missing edges are a randomized mechanistic intervention, not naturally observed exploration traces.
stopping: Fixed32groups, no exclusions or N extension. Keep original Test8b and required-irreversibility results unchanged.
